sentences.text:
Pushpendra Paserkar @ Sani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
on 20 January, 2023

Author: Anjuli Palo
Bench: Anjuli Palo
In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Cra No. 8832 of 2022
(Pushpendra Paserkar @ Sani Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) Dated : 20-01-2023
Shri Paritosh Trivedi - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Raghuveer Prajapati - Panel Lawyer for the State.

entities.text: High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No.18699/2022, an application for condonation of delay.
The appeal is barred by 21 day which is not inordinate delay.
From the reasons stated in the application, this Court finds proper reasons have been assigned and sufficient cause for condonation of delay is made out.

Hence,
I.A. No.18699 of 2022 is hereby allowed, delay in filing the appeal is condoned.
Also heard on admission.
Admit.
Also heard on I.A. No.18554/2022, which is first application filed on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

T h e appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 376(2)(n) & 506 Part-II of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.2000/- and R.I. for 1 year respectively, with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that appellant is innocent and the trial Court has not appreciated the evidence on record in proper perspective hence, arrived at erroneous findings.
It is further contended that the prosecutrix was major at the time of incident and a consenting party.
Doctor did not find any external or internal injury on her person.
The appellant is in custody since long and final disposal of appeal would take considerable time, hence, it is prayed that sentence of the appellant be suspended and he be released on bail.
Learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer for bail.
As per the prosecution case, at the time of the incident, the prosecutrix was major.
Appellant committed rape with her first time on 06.08.2017 and thereafter, he has repeatedly committed rape upon her.
She informed about the incident to her parents and thereafter FIR has been lodged against the appellant.
From the statement of the prosecutrix, it appears that she was consenting party.
Doctor did not find any sign of violence on the person of the prosecutrix.

entities.text: Pushpendra Paserkar @ Sani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 jail sentence more than 5 years and 4 months.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, custody period of the appellant and taking into account that final disposal of this appeal would take considerable time; I find it to be a fit case to suspend the custodial sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail, therefore, without commencing on the merit of the case, this application is allowed.
I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the trial Court on 07.07.2023 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
The appellant shall regularly appear before the trial Court, on each and every date, without fail.
List this matter for final hearing in due course.
